text: the worst thing a woman can do is marry a man. Statistically speaking married women do not live as long as single women they don't earn as much money as single women and they are not as happy as single women. In every single sociological study the data shows that married women are less contented. This is fact! So the lady in the video says that the worst thing a woman can do is marry a man and then she makes three claims. Claim number 1. Married women do not live as long as single women. Claim number 2. Married women do not earn as much as single women. And claim number 3. Married women are less happy and less contented, supposedly according to every single sociological study. Let's see if any of this is actually supported by evidence. Starting with life expectancy. This claim is false. Most large studies find the opposite association. Married women tend to live longer than unmarried women although the advantage is smaller than it is for men. For example a large US longitudinal study found that at age 65 married women were expected to live another 21.1 years while unmarried women were expected to live another 19.6 years. That is approximately 1.5 additional years for married women. A meta-analysis covering almost 7.9 million people also found that being unmarried was associated with higher all-cause mortality for women as well as men, although the association was stronger for men. That does not necessarily prove marriage itself causes people to live longer. Healthier and wealthier people may be more likely to marry and remain married but it definitely contradicts her claim that married women statistically die earlier. Now claim number 2. Married women do not earn as much as single women. This one is misleading. This can sometimes appear true in raw personal income statistics particularly because married mothers are more likely to reduce their hours, work part-time or temporarily leave employment. But researchers generally distinguish between a marriage penalty and a motherhood or child penalty. A US study using social security earnings records found that among women who worked the marriage earnings gap had almost disappeared for more recent generations. Among women without children married women actually earned more than single women. The large remaining difference was associated primarily with motherhood not marriage itself. A major international study published in 2025 similarly found that marriage penalties are close to zero in many high-income countries while the arrival of children produces much larger and more persistent employment penalties for women. So a fair statement would be married mothers often have lower personal earnings than childless women largely because of reduced employment and working hours after childbirth. That is very different from saying simply marrying a man makes a woman earn less. And lastly, claim number 3. Married women are less happy and less contented supposedly according to every single sociological study. This one is completely false. There is no such consensus. In fact, many studies find married women report higher not lower life satisfaction than single women. A recent European study found that people with stable marital histories had higher life satisfaction and subjective health than those who remained single or divorced. This pattern appeared among both men and women although the association was somewhat stronger for men. The more realistic finding is that relationship quality matters enormously. A 2026 longitudinal German study found people were generally happier while in a relationship than while single. A good quality relationship was better than being single but being single was better than being in a poor or moderate quality relationship. There's also evidence that some of the apparent happiness advantage is selection. People who were already happier and healthier are more likely to marry and less likely to divorce. So out of her three claims, the first is contradicted by the evidence. The second removes practically all context surrounding motherhood and employment. And the third is just demonstrably false. So is the worst thing a woman can do is marry a man? No. This is once again an anti-male rhetoric dressed up as sociology.
